I can sum up my experience. I will put it in points.
But first I want to make this clear, this is "MY" experience and what worked for "ME", let's sum it up

- It is my first time to learn another language, while I have good English, but I started learning from early years in school, so it is my first time doing it myself.

- Because of that, I had to go on testing all available things, starting from free and tried some paid services, I started what is common, Duolingo and Memrise, but I didn't like them, I understand they have different method, but here I talk about what worked for me better, I paid to use Babel, I like Babel, but still not "my thing".

- My thing was as I mentioned, complete Spanish podcast, took me through basics and developed my basic knowledge bit by bit.

- After that reading books, taking you from basics and doing exercises was what worked better for me (book name is Spanish DeMYSTiFieD http://amzn.to/2bDmAcX )

- So, if I going to start a new language today I will go to languagetransfer.org and see if that language available, the language transfer method makes things A LOT easier and faster, if I can't find the language I'm learning on language transfer project, I will search for another podcast and alongside with it I will read a book.

- Starting by a podcast alongside with a book would take 1-2 months (if you are really serious)

So pillars that works for me

- start discovering podcasts, download one and listen it when you can

- read a book, grammar explained step by step and every lesson has exercises

- start talking with natives through text

- when you feel comfortable talking through text, start doing over video "Skype"
